title: Extend the egress guard to non-provider egress (webhook delivery)
background: Model providers are not the only path content leaves the box. An audit of every outbound Req call in lib/ found: anthropic.ex:139 and embedding_client.ex:109,133 are gated by Admission; workers/content_ingestion_worker.ex:634 (Req.get of an arbitrary ingestion URL) bypasses it and is guarded instead by UrlGuard.pinned_request_opts/1 + redirect: false (:620-632); verification/github_actions.ex:17, secrets/fly_adapter.ex:60,112 and webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43 all bypass Admission entirely. Of these, webhook delivery is the one that can carry TENANT CONTENT to a TENANT-SUPPLIED URL. The 2026-07-15 draft missed this: a local_only guarantee that covers embeddings and extraction but not webhooks is not a guarantee, and stating it as one would be worse than not offering the tier.

story.as_a: a tenant who marked a scope local_only
story.i_want_to: have that marking cover EVERY path content can leave the instance, including webhook delivery
story.so_that: the guarantee I was given is the guarantee I actually have - not one that holds for two subsystems and silently fails for a third

rationale: A privacy guarantee is only as strong as its weakest egress path. Shipping US-41.4 alone would let loopctl truthfully report 'all providers local' while a webhook subscription ships article bodies to an arbitrary internet host. This story closes the gap and, just as importantly, makes the posture report honest.

acceptance_criteria.description: Webhook delivery consults the same local classification as US-41.4. For a local_only scope, a delivery whose destination is not classified local is refused before the request, with the same fail-closed semantics (unclassifiable means refuse).

A blocked delivery is NOT a silent drop and NOT an infinite retry: the event is recorded as blocked with an agent-readable reason, surfaced through the existing webhook delivery/failure surfaces, so the tenant can see that a subscription is incompatible with their local_only marking.

Creating or updating a webhook subscription with a non-local destination on an already-local_only scope is rejected AT CONFIG TIME with a legible remediation, rather than accepted and silently blocked at delivery time.

Marking a scope local_only when incompatible webhook subscriptions already exist does not silently break them: the operation either refuses with a list of the offending subscriptions or completes and reports them explicitly. Which one is chosen is documented; a silent state change is not acceptable.

egress_posture (US-41.4 AC-41.4.6) is extended to report webhook destinations and their local classification, so the posture report covers every content-carrying egress path. Until this story lands, the posture report must state that its scope is provider calls only.

The remaining outbound paths are explicitly triaged in the docs with a rationale for each: ingestion URL fetch (inbound content, sends no tenant data, already URL-guarded), GitHub verification (commit metadata only), Fly secrets (operator-plane, no tenant content). Any that DO carry tenant content are brought under the guard rather than documented away.

test_cases.name: local_only blocks a public webhook destination
preconditions: subscription pointing at a public URL
expected_results: delivery recorded as blocked with a legible reason

test_cases.name: local destination still delivers
preconditions: subscription pointing at a loopback URL

test_cases.name: incompatible subscription rejected at creation
steps: create a subscription with a public destination
expected_results: rejected with remediation naming the conflict

test_cases.name: pre-existing subscriptions surfaced when enabling local_only
preconditions: scope with a public webhook subscription
expected_results: the offending subscriptions are reported explicitly per the documented behavior - never silently disabled

test_cases.name: blocked deliveries do not retry forever
expected_results: no unbounded retry backlog - blocked is terminal for that delivery

technical_notes: webhooks/req_delivery.ex:43 uses Req.request/1 and is invoked from the delivery worker - the guard belongs where the destination is resolved, before the request is built, mirroring the provider-call placement.
Webhook signing secrets are already Cloak-encrypted (webhooks/webhook.ex:61); the destination URL is not a secret and must be readable by egress_posture.
Do not conflate 'blocked' with 'failed' in the delivery record - a blocked delivery is a configuration conflict, and an operator or agent reading failures needs to tell them apart.
AC-41.5.6 is a real audit, not a paragraph: re-run the outbound Req call inventory at implementation time, since new call sites may have landed.
